A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SASHA research work, with 23 readable pages including Appendix A.1–A.6. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–23 are identical; page 1 differs only in author names and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v4 reports original SASHA classification results on CAMELYON16 and TCGA-NSCLC in Table 1, multiclass results in Appendix Table 9, and ablation, efficiency, calibration, and sampling-behavior analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains the same original classification experiments and supplementary analyses, including Tables 1 and 9 and the appendix control experiments.

M1.justification: The HAFED feature distiller, targeted state updater, PPO agent, training objectives, and inference procedure are identical in Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same binary tasks on CAMELYON16 and TCGA-NSCLC and multiclass tasks on Camelyon+ and BRACS. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including the full-slide MIL methods, RLogist, and Zoom-MIL in Table 1 and ACMIL/DTFD comparisons in Appendix Tables 9–10.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, metrics, sampling budgets, training settings, and testing procedures are identical in Section 4 and Appendices A.1–A.4.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, limited-budget comparisons, alternative inference policies and reward schedules, calibration analyses, and tumor-localization case study in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is identical, including Table 10's means and standard deviations across five splits and three sampling seeds, Figure 4's standard-deviation bands, and Figure 3's significance annotations.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports SASHA-0.2 CAMELYON16 accuracy of 0.953 ± 0.017 in both versions; appendix results and plotted findings also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations are identical, including the state/action definitions, cumulative tumor-patch hit ratio in Equation (1), and compressibility definition in Appendix A.4. No proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about selective sampling, diagnostic performance, computational savings, and the contributions of HAFED, TSU, and the RL agent.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sampling behavior and calibration remain identical. Section 5 and Appendix A.6 retain the same limitations concerning training cost, fixed budgets, architecture overhead, sparse tumors, and clinical domain shift.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, hyperparameters, training details, hardware disclosures, and the implementation repository link are unchanged. Only the document's own arXiv version link changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, all 41 references, and the positioning relative to prior MIL, reinforcement-learning, and feature-extraction approaches are identical.

P1.justification: On page 1, 'Tarun G' becomes 'Tarun Gogisetty' and 'Devarajan Sridharan' becomes 'Sridharan Devarajan'; the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5, Tables 1–13, Algorithm 1, their captions, and their placement are identical. The author and version-stamp edits do not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: v5 updates author-name presentation and the version/date stamp, while retaining identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility details throughout the main text and appendix. These administrative edits do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
